target_customer: Consumers and bloggers who wanted quick edits to web photos without installing desktop software; later publishers embedding the editor through an API
problem: Editing a photo required desktop software such as Photoshop. Snipshot let people crop, resize, adjust colors and auto-enhance a photo in the browser, starting from a one-click bookmarklet, then save it back to the web.
business_model: Free consumer web app with an embeddable editor API; advertising and API licensing implied but not sourced

founders.name: Beau Hartshorne
founders.background_notes: YC profile says he later joined Facebook as an early employee working on growth, photos and mobile, and holds several patents.

founders.name: Greg Dingle
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page with no further biography.

competitors.name: Picnik
competitors.what: Flash-based online photo editor with Flickr style integrations
competitors.traction_then: Launched early 2007, so it arrived about a year after the batch; TechCrunch called it a favorite replacing PXN8

competitors.name: PXN8
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch in 2007 as the previous favorite online editor

technical_complexity.rationale: Server side image processing in the browser era before HTML5 canvas was common, plus a bookmarklet and an embeddable API. Standard engineering for one strong developer, with scaling image workloads as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Features were easy to copy, and several editors (Picnik, PXN8, Pixlr) launched within a year. No network effect or data lock in is described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The YC description itself says Photoshop planned to enter the category. Later, Picnik was a closer rival, and Google was reported elsewhere to have consolidated online photo editing; no source here shows an incumbent killing Snipshot.

market_need_then: Mid 2000s growth of digital cameras and photo blogging created demand for quick edits without desktop software; a Christian Science Monitor column from November 2006 covered web photo editors as an emerging category.

branding.domain_note: Operated on snipshot.com, the exact .com; the site returned HTTP 503 when fetched in 2026.

brand_strength.rationale: Mentioned in a 2006 newspaper column and in 2007 comparisons with Picnik, but no source shows press about the brand itself, merch or community.

outcome_analysis: Snipshot was an early browser photo editor in the Winter 2006 batch and found an exit, being sold to Ansa in 2013 per YC. The terms and the shutdown cause are not public. A wave of similar tools from 2007 onward, Picnik most visibly, and later mobile photo apps likely squeezed a low moat product, but this is inference rather than something a source states.
notes: Directory status is Inactive while the YC page also says it was sold to Ansa in 2013, so exit is recorded as acquisition. No funding found in two searches; a Crunchbase entry named snipshot.io appears to be a different product. Competitor sources are dated 2006-11 to 2007-02, slightly after the batch. Failure factors are inferred from the competitive record and are low confidence. A Dealroom listing names Ansa but not Snipshot.
